purpose: G2's own cases: each justifies one canonicalization exclusion, or proves an exclusion was NOT made. Kept separate from G0's frozen corpus so G0's digest and acceptance stay valid.

cases.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::usesPrivate
cases.note: JUSTIFIES body exclusion #2. A local's name is not observable, so encoding locals by binding ordinal is safe. Compared against g2_local_base rather than base, because base writes the member as an arrow expression with no local at all -- comparing against it would measure a shape change, not a rename.

cases.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::usesPrivate
cases.note: PROVES order is NOT excluded. Execution order is observable, so the body fingerprint must move. If this case reported body_equal the canonicalizer would be discarding something that changes behaviour.

cases.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::Box
cases.dimension: a type parameter is renamed T -> S
cases.note: JUSTIFIES the ABI exclusion. A type parameter's name is not observable at a call site; position and bound are what a caller depends on.

cases.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::pick
cases.dimension: which FORMAL PARAMETER the body returns: a -> b
cases.note: The body walk used to start at f.body, so formals never entered the local table and every reference encoded as VarGet#-1 -- making `=> a` and `=> b` identical. Formals are now registered in declaration order, and an unregistered variable is a refusal rather than an ordinal.

cases.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::topConst
cases.note: The field body used to record only whether an initializer existed, so `final x = 1` -> `final x = 2` stayed equal. The initializer expression is now encoded.

cases.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::Shape.square
cases.note: Initializer lists are separate Kernel structure and are not reachable from function.body, so this change vanished entirely. Constructors now encode c.initializers.

cases.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::Box.unwrap
cases.dimension: the OWNER's generic bound moves while the member's own signature reads T -> T
cases.note: G1 deferred the owner/type relationship here. Box.unwrap's own signature is unchanged, so its ABI is equal -- but reuse still must be refused, because the owner's ABI moved. The row carries owner_abi_fingerprint and the classifier requires BOTH to match.

cases.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::looped
cases.dimension: the body uses a node kind OUTSIDE the allowlist (a for loop)
cases.note: The refusal must be REACHABLE and expected, not merely representable. The classifier returns refused:unsupported_body before any equality check, and reuse requires BOTH baseline and variant encodings to be supported -- an unsupported baseline is just as disqualifying.

cases.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::Box.unwrap
cases.dimension: two libraries each declare a Box; only corpus.other's bound moves
cases.note: app's Box is UNTOUCHED, so its member's owner ABI must not move. With the owner table keyed by bare class name, corpus.other's Box overwrote corpus.app's and this member would inherit the wrong contract.

cases.subject: package:corpus/other.dart::Box.unwrap
cases.dimension: the SAME member name in the library whose Box bound did move
cases.note: Same class name, same member name, different library: this one's owner ABI must move. The pair only passes if the owner table is library-qualified.

cases.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::looped
cases.note: reversed direction: the BASELINE is the unencodable side. classify() originally read only the variant's body_status, so an unencodable OLD body compared against a clean new one would have been classified on body equality. Reuse compares two encodings; either being incomplete makes 'equal' mean 'equal in the parts I looked at'.
